description: Figure 6(b) illustrates how the hyperparameter \(N\) affects AUC (%) for five methods (SMD, PSM, SWaT, SMAP, and MSL). The x-axis is labeled \(N\) on a linear scale, spanning from 1 to 20 with tick marks at 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “AUC (%)” on a linear scale, ranging from 70 to 100 with labeled ticks at 70, 80, 90, and 100. Five solid lines with distinct markers are shown: SMD is an orange line with square markers, rising from about 85 at \(N=1\) to about 95 at \(N=10\), peaking near 98 at \(N=15\), then decreasing to about 92 at \(N=20\); PSM is a blue line with circular markers, increasing from about 92 at \(N=1\) to about 98 at \(N=10\), then declining to about 95 at \(N=20\); SWaT is a green line with upward-triangle markers, increasing from about 88 at \(N=1\) to about 96 at \(N=10\), then decreasing to about 94 at \(N=20\); SMAP is a magenta line with downward-triangle markers, starting near 74 at \(N=1\), increasing to about 95 at \(N=10\), then decreasing to about 78 at \(N=20\); MSL is a yellow line with diamond markers, increasing from about 82 at \(N=1\) to about 97 at \(N=15\), then decreasing to about 93 at \(N=20\).
